metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Can Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton come from the back again as Lando Norris hopes for rain to fight Kimi Antonelli | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Can Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton come from the back again as Lando Norris hopes for rain to fight Kimi Antonelli Lando Norris starts on pole in Brazil from Kimi Antonelli but there will be plenty of attention further down the field with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton starting at the back; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Saturday 7 November 2026 23:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Grand Prix A mixed up grid and rain on the forecast has set up the prospect of a thrilling Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday. For the third year in a row, Lando Norris will start on pole position in Brazil with new F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli alongside him on the front row. Unusually though, there will be plenty of attention further down the field as power unit changes for Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton mean they start at the back, while Ferrari's Charles Leclerc starts 14th for a 10-grid place penalty. messages.text: Norris claims Sao Paulo GP pole after treacherous rain-hit qualifying

metadata.summary: Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Lando Norris claims rain-hit pole in wild conditions with Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen to start at back | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Lando Norris claims rain-hit pole in wild conditions with Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen to start at back Lando Norris tames awful wet conditions for his third Brazil pole in a row; Frustrated Russell drops down from second with grid penalty; Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen starting 20th and 21st; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo GP live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm By James Galloway at Interlagos Saturday 7 November 2026 23:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Grand Prix. Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid. On a rain-hit day at ever-unpredictable Interlagos, qualifying was suspended for over an hour and 20 minutes after a torrential downpour hit the drivers' first laps of Q1. The rain eventually eased - but never particularly stopped - to allow running to take place, creating a thrilling and unpredictable battle for pole. messages.text: 'Very disappointed' Russell says Mercedes error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole

metadata.summary: George Russell said he was "really disappointed" as he insisted a "misjudgement" by his Mercedes team had cost him pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: George Russell: 'Very disappointed' Mercedes driver says team error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole in chaotic wet qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: 'Very disappointed' Mercedes driver says team error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole in chaotic wet qualifying George Russell was beaten to pole for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris; Russell believes Mercedes' instruction for him to abort a flying lap cost him pole; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm Saturday 7 November 2026 22:37, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell was seething after being told to back off at a time when he believed he could have pushed for P1 during the Q3 session in Sao Paulo George Russell said he was "really disappointed" as he insisted a "misjudgement" by his Mercedes team had cost him pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Russell drove impressively throughout a hugely-challenging wet qualifying session at Interlagos but ultimately missed out on pole position by two tenths to McLaren's Lando Norris. The Mercedes driver had led Norris by four tenths of a second after their first runs in Q3, but was then told to abort his second run when he was being held up by the Williams of Alex Albon. metadata.summary: Cheavon Clarke scored a stunning stoppage win over Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London.
metadata.content: Cheavon Clarke hands Chris Billam-Smith first stoppage loss in stunning upset win over former world champion | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Cheavon Clarke hands Chris Billam-Smith first stoppage loss in stunning upset win over former world champion Cheavon Clarke beat former world champion Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London; Billam-Smith had never been dropped before but Clarke put him over twice before the referee halted the Bournemouth star John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Saturday 7 November 2026 23:30, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Zuffa Boxing 12 cruiserweight main event between Chev Clarke and Chris Billam-Smith and Chev Clarke Cheavon Clarke scored a stunning stoppage win over Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London. He not only knocked the former world champion down for the first time in Billam-Smith's career, he put him over twice and handed the Bournemouth star a first stoppage defeat. Halted on the ropes, as Clarke's right hooks streaked in, Billam-Smith at once shook his head to protest as the referee waved it off. Clarke, after a thrilling win over Jack Massey last time out, was looking for a big-name scalp that would launch him into the top class of the division. He got it. Mosley would have been happy with the opening round. He took the centre of the ring and used his long left to marshal Bentley. Pressed into a corner and backed up, Bentley threw potshots. messages.text: 'A different Noni?' Madueke finding a new level for Arsenal

metadata.summary: Noni Madueke lay sprawled on the turf, head in his hands, following his one-on-one miss late in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Hull. His frustration continued to show even after the final whistle.
metadata.content: Noni Madueke has become a 'different' player, says Mikel Arteta, as winger finds new level of creativity and efficiency | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Noni Madueke has become a 'different' player, says Mikel Arteta, as winger finds new level of creativity and efficiency Noni Madueke starred in Arsenal's 1-0 win over Hull as the Gunners moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League; former Chelsea winger is creating more chances than anyone else in the division and has become a "different" player, says Mikel Arteta Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Saturday 7 November 2026 22:08, UK Image: Noni Madueke helped Arsenal claim a 1-0 win over Hull Noni Madueke lay sprawled on the turf, head in his hands, following his one-on-one miss late in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Hull . His frustration continued to show even after the final whistle. The winger's reaction showed the standards this "different Noni", to quote Mikel Arteta, is setting himself as he strives to reach another level. Bukayo Saka's injury was a significant setback to Arsenal. Madueke has made it his mission to soften the blow. So far, he has filled in impressively. Arteta understood his demeanour after the game. "He knew he had three clear chances to score," he said, always demanding more. But there was also an acknowledgement of his crucial role in Martin Odegaard's goal.
